deep.reconstruction:
Context. Cote 80 develops a purely combinatorial axiomatics for 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', meaning arrangements of pseudo-lines in the (real projective) plane. The goal is to recover the topological (cellular) structure from incidence and order data.

The objects ρ_{D,s}. The machine transcription's '∫D̄,s' is almost certainly ρ_{\vec D, s}, the same symbol as on the previous page.
- Each ρ_{\vec D,s} is defined at a vertex s (an intersection point) and indexed by oriented pseudo-lines \vec D through s.
- It is a local 'rotation' operator. It acts on oriented pseudo-lines through s, or equivalently on flags (s, u, u') given by triangles s u_1 u'_1.
- Axiom (e), previous page: rotating at s sends the triangle (s u_1 u'_1) to (s u_2 u'_2) when u_1, u_2 are adjacent on \vec D. This is a compatibility between the order of points along pseudo-lines and the rotation at s.
- Axiom (f), previous page: if s has order 2n (n pseudo-lines through s, so 2n half-branches), then (ρ_{\vec D,s})^n(\vec Z) = -\vec Z. Turning half way round reverses orientation, as for a rotation by π.

In modern terms, the data {ρ_s} is a rotation system: a cyclic order of the half-edges at each vertex. Together with the linear or cyclic order of vertices along each pseudo-line, it determines the 2-cell embedding of the arrangement graph in RP^2 (Heffter–Edmonds–Ringel principle).

The theorem on this page. Suppose a system of ρ_{\vec D,s} exists satisfying a)–f). Suppose also the arrangement contains no 'degenerate' pseudo-lines, meaning monogons or digons: pseudo-lines carrying only one or two vertices, whose cyclic structure gives no orientation information. Then the system of ρ's is unique, i.e. the local rotation data is forced by the incidence/order data.

Moreover, the system of unoriented local data Ω(s) = {ρ_s, ρ_s^{-1}} (my reading of '{ρ_s, ρ_s''}': the pair of mutually inverse rotations, forgetting the choice of turning direction) forms in a unique way a 'local system' satisfying [sentence breaks off]. Passing from ρ to the pair {ρ, ρ^{-1}} is exactly passing to what makes sense on a non-orientable surface like RP^2. There a global choice of turning direction is impossible, but the unordered pair is a well-defined local system.

Marginal note (written diagonally):
- Only e), f) and a) (in the 'sans digones' situation) are actually needed for uniqueness.
- To make sense of the local system, further axioms (a), b), and a new g)) will have to be assumed.
- A crossed-out fragment follows.

This shows Grothendieck pruning his axiom list and anticipating an extra axiom g), which does not appear on this page.

What the page serves. It is a rigidity/uniqueness statement: the combinatorial 'pseudo-plane' structure determines the local cyclic structure at vertices. This is the key step for proving that an abstract axiomatic system of pseudo-lines comes from a unique cell structure on the projective plane.
errors: The statement is only sketched: no proof on this page, and the second statement ('De plus ...') is cut off.

The non-degeneracy hypothesis is phrased loosely ('ps. droites qui sont des monogônes ou digônes'). If it means cells rather than pseudo-lines, it is vacuous for genuine projective arrangements of ≥3 non-concurrent pseudo-lines, since all cells then have ≥3 sides. So it most plausibly means pseudo-lines carrying ≤2 vertices.
The margin itself flags that the axiom list a)–f) is redundant for uniqueness and insufficient for the local-system statement (g) is needed). So the theorem as written is not in final form.

ideas.what: Local rotation operators ρ_{D,s} at vertices of a pseudo-line arrangement, axiomatized via compatibility with orders along lines and ρ^n = -1 at a vertex of order 2n
ideas.modern_name: rotation system / combinatorial map structure on the arrangement graph (cf. Grothendieck's own 'cartes' in Esquisse)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heffter (1891), Edmonds (1960), Ringel/Youngs (rotation systems); for arrangements, Goodman–Pollack, Folkman–Lawrence
ideas.where_published: The general philosophy of maps as permutation data is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The pseudo-line axiomatics itself is not in published texts as far as I know.

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the local rotation data given line-order data, under a non-degeneracy hypothesis (no lines with ≤2 vertices)
ideas.modern_name: rigidity of the embedding: local sequences determine the arrangement; analogous to Whitney's uniqueness of embeddings of 3-connected planar graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (local sequences, early-mid 1980s); Whitney (1933) for graphs; oriented matroid theory (Folkman–Lawrence 1978)

ideas.what: Passing to the unordered pair {ρ_s, ρ_s^{-1}} to get a canonically defined 'local system' on a non-orientable surface
ideas.modern_name: local orientation system / orientation double cover data for maps on non-orientable surfaces (generalized maps with flags)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lins (1982), Tutte; generalized maps / flag systems

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic reconstruction of the cell structure of a pseudo-line arrangement from line-order data, via vertex rotations. He notes that a)–f) are partly redundant and that an extra axiom g) is needed for the local-system statement; the thread is left incomplete here.
missed.quote: il suffit en fait e), f) et (ss droites) a) ... pour pouvoir donner un sens au syst. local, il faudra en sus supposer a) b) g)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minimal-axiom characterization of when abstract 'pseudo-plane' order data comes from a unique arrangement, contemporaneous with Goodman–Pollack's local-sequence work. A specialist might compare the axiom list, but such characterizations exist in oriented-matroid literature, so novelty is modest.

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats pseudo-line arrangements through the same permutation/rotation-system lens he later uses for combinatorial maps (dessins). This implicitly links rank-3 oriented matroids with his 'cartes' formalism, including the non-orientable case via the pairs {ρ, ρ^{-1}}.
missed.quote: le syst. des Ω(s) = {ρ_s, ρ_s''} — en forme unique un syst. local
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The literatures on pseudo-line arrangements and on maps/dessins rarely interact. Viewing the arrangement as a map on RP^2 with its oriented double cover on S^2 is natural but seldom exploited systematically.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but expected rigidity/uniqueness statement for local rotation data of pseudo-line arrangements. It is close to known results (embedding uniqueness, Goodman–Pollack local sequences, Folkman–Lawrence). Its main interest is historical: Grothendieck's independent combinatorial axiomatization circa 1981, linked to his maps viewpoint.
transcription_corrections: '∫\overline{D}_{,s}' should be read 'ρ_{\vec D, s}' (the rotation operators of the previous page), in both occurrences.
'Ω(s) = {s_1, s_0''}' is likely 'Ω(s) = {ρ_s, ρ_s^{-1}}' or '{ρ_s, ρ_s''}' — a pair of mutually inverse local rotations.
'en (le) forme unique' is probably 'en forme(nt) de façon unique' / 'forment de façon unique un syst. local satisfaisant'.
